content: 1. Learn how to effectively prevent Zika virus infection by avoiding mosquito bites and minimizing the risk of sexual transmission. 2. Understand the necessary precautions to prevent Zika virus infection when traveling to or residing in areas where the virus is prevalent. 3. Familiarize yourself with the symptoms of Zika virus infection and the potential complications it may cause. 4. Gain knowledge about congenital Zika syndrome and other birth defects that can result from Zika virus infection during pregnancy. 5. Review the annual aggregated data on reported Zika virus cases within the United States. 6. Identify the countries and territories where there is a significant risk of Zika virus transmission. 7. Learn about the criteria for determining who may require testing for Zika virus infection. 8. For healthcare professionals, review detailed information on the clinical signs and symptoms associated with Zika virus disease. 9. Access guidelines for healthcare providers on the appropriate methods for treating and preventing Zika virus disease. 10. Educate patients on strategies to prevent the sexual transmission of the Zika virus. 11. Review clinical guidelines for testing and diagnosing Zika virus disease in patients. 12. Monitor and manage pregnant patients who may have been exposed to the Zika virus during pregnancy, with a focus on clinical considerations and potential risks.
